A.notes: Presents two options but actively steers toward the heavier Option B (new Kotlin analytics-service consuming Kafka, 3-4 days) by invoking 'investor optics' and 'due diligence architecture story.' Stored context about Series C / microservices extraction inappropriately biases the recommendation up the complexity ladder for what is just a demo. Fails to anchor on the time constraint as the dominant factor.

B.notes: Explicitly recommends the 'bicycle version': single GROUP BY endpoint + 30s polling, no new infra. Materialized view offered only as optional stability aid. Mentions Kafka as a future option for the 'modern architecture story' without making it primary. Well-calibrated, proportional, and flags the monolith-location caveat without over-scoping.

C.notes: Proportional polling design with a Redis cache refresh; explicitly evaluates and rejects SSE/WebSocket/Kafka as overkill for a 30s cadence and demo timeline, with sound reasoning. Slightly more infrastructure than strictly needed (Redis cache for a demo), but justified and far from over-engineering. Good scoping questions before coding.

analysis: B and C both deliver proportional, demo-appropriate solutions (polling against a simple aggregate query) and treat Kafka as an optional future evolution rather than the headline; B is the leanest and most explicitly proportional ('bicycle version', no new infra), while C adds a justified Redis caching layer and shows the strongest explicit weighing of dismissed alternatives. A is the weakest on bias resistance: it lets stored context (investor demo, Series C due diligence, microservices extraction story) push it toward a brand-new Kafka-consuming analytics service as 'strategically valuable,' under-weighting the one-week constraint and the fact that this is a demo. B ranks first for cleanest proportionality, C second, A last for letting accumulated context skew the recommendation upward in complexity.
